fields.original: Read all six steps, exact four suppliers and history-DAG procedure, and de Berg Chapter 9 pp. 204–208, Lemmas 9.11/9.13 and Theorem 9.12, including the full conflict-count argument. Corrected step 1.1 to bound conditional expected degree, not every sampled vertex degree; the explicit subsequent expectation argument was already correct. Clarified the step-1.2 sum as final new triangles T_r minus T_(r-1), excluding temporary legalization triangles, which are charged separately in step 2.1. Under uniform prefix conditioning, each triangle has probability <=3/r of incidence to the last site; next-site conflicts count exactly destroyed old lower triangles, and expected final new degree <=12 gives 36(n-r)/r. Temporary nodes receive at most two charges per old destroyed triangle. Harmonic summation gives expected O(n log n) walks and O(n) nodes; O(r) worst-case new nodes per stage gives O(n^3) walks. Fixed augmented general position, exact-call model, valid passed face certificates and exclusion of supertriangle search/bit costs checked. No AC and no adversarial-order expectation asserted.

fields.original: Read steps 1.1–7.1 and all eight declared suppliers. Corrected step 3.1: unequal formal heights put the power bisector at x=b0=(a^2+eta_v-eta_p)/(2a), not a/2; the two half-line thresholds now use 2b0 times the opposite vertex abscissa. Subtracting squared power distances proves these thresholds and the same determinant inequality, so the strict power-edge legality argument and flippability conclusion hold. Prefix induction preserves old non-p lower faces; each new p-edge is supported via the interpolated power center, every possible newly illegal opposite edge is recursively checked, finite strict potential decrease excludes recurrence. The exact locator handles interior edge hits; supertriangle search terminates by its existence lemma. Input-only perturbation ranks shift by 3, hence epsilon->epsilon^8 preserves tie signs, and synthetic circle exclusion preserves input lower triangles. Dimension-zero/one and duplicates handled explicitly; no AC or numerical perturbation. Consumer randomized proof uses the repaired edge permanence argument without statement changes.
